son、bolero、ranchera、polka 的律動差別很大，重音位置與低: The groove of a son, a bolero, a ranchera and a polka differs a lot: the accents fall in different places and the bass patterns are not the same. A band has to switch between these song types within one evening, and that is where the real technique of this line-up lies.
一至數支，負責高音與大聲段落，與小提琴交替: One to several, carrying the high register and the loud passages, alternating with the violins
二至數把齊奏，負責歌唱性的長線條與前奏: Two or more playing in unison, carrying the singing long lines and the introductions
人聲與樂器共用同一種和聲習慣：兩聲部常以三度或六度平行進行，小號與小提琴的齊奏也: Voices and instruments share the same harmonic habit: the two parts usually move in parallel thirds or sixths, and the trumpet and the violin often stack in unison the same way. That parallel third is a sound common to Mexican traditional and popular music, and it feels like one block moving rather than counterpoint between independent parts.
以根音與五度交替撐出每小節的重心，是整團的時間地板: Holds up the centre of each bar by alternating root and fifth; the time floor of the whole band
先說節奏。以 son jalisciense 為例，墨西哥大吉他在小節的重拍上給: Start with the rhythm. In a son jalisciense, for example, the guitarrón gives the root on the strong beat of the bar and moves to the fifth on the weak beat; the two notes alternate back and forth and make up the time floor of the whole band. The vihuela does not play those bass notes: it strums the chords between one beat and the next, so it sounds like it is pushing the beat rather than striking it. Put the two together and the skeleton of the beat is clear even with no drum.
先鎖定墨西哥大吉他的兩音交替：根音在哪、五度在哪，那就是整團的時鐘。: Fix on the guitarrón's two-note alternation first: where the root is, where the fifth is. That is the band's clock.
其他曲種會改寫這個分工。bolero 慢、分句長，大吉他的低音型放慢、變得更連續: Other song types rewrite this division of work. A bolero is slow with long phrases, so the guitarrón's bass pattern slows and becomes more continuous, and the vihuela's strumming stretches with it; a ranchera can be very slow or very fast, and when it is slow the instruments pull back and fill in at the ends of phrases; huapango uses syncopation to shift the accents; once polka and cumbia came onto the stage repertoire, the centre of gravity of the bass pattern shifted again. What lets a band switch between these song types in one evening is not a change of instruments but the same set of instruments changing the rhythmic structure, the accent placement and the density of the bass pattern with the song type.
再聽維瑞拉琴的刷弦位置。它幾乎都落在拍點的空隙，而不是正拍上；這個「推」的感覺是: Listen next to where the vihuela strums. It almost always lands in the gaps between beats rather than on the beat; that sense of pushing is the core of Mexican rhythm.
協調方式很直接：沒有指揮。領班通常是第一小提琴或大吉他手，他用眼神、點頭、一句喊: Coordination is direct: there is no conductor. The leader is usually the first violin or the guitarrón player; he starts things with a look, a nod or a shout, and section changes are signalled by fixed introductions and closing phrases (remates) that tell everyone when to stop. Because most bands work from hearing and from a fixed memory of the sections rather than from a score, a piece can be lengthened or shortened on the spot: the singer adds a verse, the players go round once more, depending on the occasion and the audience.
同樣是原聲、不插電的小型樂隊，藍草樂隊與墨西哥流浪樂隊最容易被放在一起，但兩者的: Both are acoustic, unamplified small bands, so bluegrass and mariachi are the easiest pair to put side by side, yet their division of work runs opposite ways. In bluegrass the beat is held up by the mandolin's chop and by the double bass's root on the first beat and fifth on the third, the players line up on one rhythmic grid, and when someone solos the others fall back to accompaniment; mariachi has no drum, the time is made jointly by the guitarrón's root–fifth alternation and the vihuela's strumming, and the melodic layer (violins and trumpets) is out front almost from beginning to end, with none of bluegrass's stretches where improvised solos are the spine of the structure and everyone else falls back to accompaniment for long periods.
和管樂團相比，差別在編制與音量策略。管樂團靠人數與聲部分工取得平衡，有指揮、有總: Compared with a wind band, the difference lies in the line-up and the strategy for volume. A wind band balances through numbers and a division into sections, with a conductor and a full score, woodwind, brass and percussion each forming a family; mariachi is usually around ten players, with no conductor, no scores, section changes carried by the leader's eye and by fixed introductions and closing phrases (remates), the key decided by the singer, and the balance obtained from the instruments' own projection rather than dialled in by a conductor.
墨西哥流浪樂隊就是「墨西哥音樂」，一定是十幾人的大編制、全員穿查羅服、以小號為主: Mariachi is "Mexican music": it must be a big line-up of a dozen or more, all in charro dress, led by trumpets.
墨西哥流浪樂隊（Mariachi）— 以小提琴與小號奏旋律、維瑞拉與大吉他撐節奏: Mariachi — a Mexican band line-up with violins and trumpets carrying the melody and vihuela and guitarrón holding the rhythm. Ensembles and instrumentation by Next Door Sound Weavers.
墨西哥流浪樂隊（mariachi）用幾把小提琴與小號奏旋律，用維瑞拉琴（vihu: Mariachi plays the melody on a few violins and trumpets and holds rhythm and bass with the vihuela mexicana and the guitarrón, working at weddings, birthdays, coming-of-age parties and funerals. It is a line-up that plays at your front door: every instrument is acoustic, and it has to be heard in a courtyard or a plaza without amplification.
它是墨西哥西部的地域傳統。小號到二十世紀才加入，核心其實是弦樂；今日舞臺上整齊劃: It is a regional tradition of western Mexico. The trumpet only joined in the twentieth century; the core is really the strings. The uniform dress and the large line-up seen on stage today are a format fixed by film, television and the tourist industry. Bands at village and family occasions are much smaller, and do not necessarily include a trumpet.
常以三度或六度平行唱，句尾加上喊聲: Usually sung in parallel thirds or sixths, with a shout at the end of the phrase
所有曲子都是同一種節奏，只是快慢不同。: Every piece has the same rhythm, only faster or slower.
找 son jalisciense 的錄音，試著把同一組低音同時數成兩大拍與三大: Find a recording of a son jalisciense and try counting the same bass figure both in two big beats and in three; once you can do it, you will hear the flexibility of this music.
找現場錄音而不是錄音室版本。原音編制在庭院與廣場裡的平衡，和錄音室混出來的平衡是: Look for a live recording rather than a studio one. The balance an acoustic line-up reaches in a courtyard or a plaza is a different thing from the balance mixed in a studio.
旋律層的分工也是「輪流」而非「一起」。典型做法是：前奏由小提琴或小號單獨出來，歌: The division of work in the melodic layer is also taking turns rather than playing together. The usual pattern: the introduction comes from the violin or the trumpet alone, during the singing the brass pulls back to fill in at the ends of phrases, and the whole band comes in on the chorus. The violin supplies the singing long line, the trumpet supplies the high register and the volume; the two rarely play the same melody together from beginning to end — when timbre and range overlap they blur each other's line, so traditional arranging has them lead in turn to keep the layers apart.
曲目與段落是固定的：前奏、歌唱、間奏、收尾都有約定的位置。樂手在現場調整的是長度: The repertoire and the sections are fixed: introduction, singing, interlude and close all have agreed places. What the players adjust on the spot is length and volume, not harmony or structure.
曲目類型包括 son jalisciense、ranchera、bolero、h: The types include son jalisciense, ranchera, bolero, huapango, polka, cumbia and the march-like pasodoble. A band usually does not sort its repertoire by type but by occasion: what is needed for the entrance, what for the toast, what to see the guests off. That is why one band's list runs across several rhythms, and why the players have to switch bodily feel again and again in a single evening.
最典型的場合是 serenata：清晨或深夜在窗下、庭院裡演奏，壽星或情人站在陽: The most typical occasion is the serenata: playing under a window or in a courtyard at dawn or late at night, with the person being celebrated or the lover standing on the balcony listening. This form of playing at the door dictates that the line-up be light, unamplified and ready to start at any moment. Weddings, fifteenth-birthday celebrations, birthdays, Mother's Day, religious festivals and funerals all need it too; a funeral reverses the festive use, with the band slowing down and drawing in, the music there to accompany rather than to celebrate.
樂隊以一個共同的參考音對齊，弦樂器之間先互相對好，小號再對上去；在戶外，溫度與濕: The band tunes to one shared reference note, the strings matching each other first and the trumpet then matching them; outdoors, temperature and humidity keep pulling the strings out, so retuning at the interval is normal. To change key, the guitar and vihuela move the same chord shape up with a capo, while the violin and trumpet change position or fingering. The key is decided by the singer and the band follows him — the same piece can sit in a completely different key with a different singer.
歌唱與銅管之間還有一種呼應：歌手唱完一句，小號在同一個和聲位置上重複或回應那句話: There is another kind of answer between the singing and the brass: when the singer finishes a line, the trumpet repeats or answers the tail of that line on the same harmony. This is not an added decoration but a way of stretching the length of a melodic line, giving the singer room to breathe and letting the brass take over where there are no words. Listen for it: the trumpet rarely cuts in mid-phrase; it almost always lands at the end.
聽小提琴與小號的交接，注意同一段旋律很少由同一組樂器從頭吹到尾。: Listen for the handover between violin and trumpet, and notice how rarely one melody is carried by one group of instruments from beginning to end.
補中低頻與刷弦厚度，穩住和聲: Fills in the low midrange and the thickness of the strumming, steadying the harmony
調音與換調也是分工的一部分。: Tuning and key changes are part of the division of work too.
這三層之所以是這些樂器而不是別的，和音量有關。墨西哥大吉他的琴身大、弦粗，能在不: These three layers are these instruments rather than others because of volume. The guitarrón has a big body and thick strings, and can give enough low end without amplification; the vihuela is smaller than a guitar and its strumming is short and crisp, exactly filling the space between the violins and the guitarrón; the trumpet is one of the most efficient projectors among acoustic instruments, and outdoors it can carry a melody to the back of a crowd. Put together, the three amount to an amplification system that needs no electricity.
這個編制的邏輯不是交響樂式的分聲部，而是「一條旋律、兩層刷弦、一條低音」的疊法。: The logic of this line-up is not symphonic part-writing but a stack of one melody, two layers of strumming and one bass line. The melody is carried by violin and trumpet in turn, the harmony and syncopation by the vihuela, the bass and the beat by the guitarrón, and the voice sits on top of the melody. Every instrument is acoustic, because the band's workplace is a doorway, a courtyard, a cemetery and a plaza, not a concert hall.
這個骨架有一個容易被忽略的特性：son jalisciense 的低音型在 6/: This skeleton has a property that is easily missed: the bass pattern of the son jalisciense swings between two groupings, 6/8 and 3/4. The same set of notes can be counted as two big beats or as three; singers and dancers each take what they need, so the same piece can be sung at ease or danced at speed. This double grouping is not vagueness but exactly where the flexibility of the genre lies: the players use one bass pattern and serve both tempos.
高音域刷弦，把和弦打在拍點之間，製造推進感: Strumming in the upper register, putting the chords between the beats to create a sense of drive
